newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORWAY SIGNS GAS SALES DEAL WITH CZECH REPUBLIC.
newsitem.headline: NORWAY SIGNS GAS SALES DEAL WITH CZECH REPUBLIC.

text.p: Norway has signed an agreement to supply gas to the Czech Republic, its first gas export deal with an eastern European country, Norway's minister of industry and energy Jens Stoltenberg said on Wednesday.
Under the agreement with Czech state gas company Transgas, first deliveries will begin on Jan 1 1997, ramping up to a 20 year plateau level of three billion cubic meters a year by 2002.

"Although volumes are small compared to total Norwegian volumes in Europe, this shows we are in a position to supply gas to the former communist countries of central and eastern Europe," Stoltenberg told delegates at an oil and gas conference in Stavanger.

Norwegian gas exports to Europe are set to reach 60 billion cubic meters a year early in the next century, but the eastern European gas market has traditionally been the exclusive domain of Russian gas giant Gazprom.
The agreement still has to be approved by Czech authorities.
Stoltenberg said the gas supplies would mainly substitute the use of coal in households and the small industrial sector, but could eventually be used for power generation.
